mixed.task: Fix the React request waterfall and the Postgres pagination query.
The React page fetches user and posts one after the other, and the Postgres report gets slower on deep pages.
Our Next.js page awaits each fetch in sequence. Separately, deleting a customer in Postgres scans the whole orders table.
Build a scalable Next.js application with PostgreSQL, Redis caching, JWT authentication, and optimized database queries.
Our FastAPI service writes to Postgres and the endpoint blocks because we use a sync driver inside async def.
The Django app on Kubernetes drops requests during every rollout and the ORM issues hundreds of queries per page.
Our React Native app stores the JWT in AsyncStorage and the FlatList of orders stutters.
The Express API uses MongoDB and someone logged in by sending an object as the password; also errors in async routes crash the server.
Our Go service on Docker has a 1.5GB image and its http client never times out.
The Vue frontend talks to a GraphQL API that runs one SQL query per item in the list.
We deploy a Spring Boot service with Terraform; the plan wants to recreate the database and the JPA list page is slow from lazy loading.
Our RAG chatbot uses pgvector in Postgres; exact product codes are never found and answers cite documents from other tenants.
The Angular app calls a Rails API; the search box shows stale results and the Rails endpoint loads authors one by one.
GitHub Actions builds our Docker image on every push and reinstalls all npm packages each time.
Our Flask app uses SQLite; writes fail with database is locked and the app was deployed with debug on.
A Kotlin Android app syncs with a REST API; the app freezes when loading data and retried uploads create duplicates.
Our TypeScript Node service on AWS Lambda exhausts the RDS connection limit during traffic bursts.
The SwiftUI app talks to a GraphQL backend; the view model resets on every update and a nested query took the server down.
We cache MySQL query results in Redis and users see old prices after an update.
Our Next.js app uses Tailwind; the dynamic badge colors are missing in production and a server action deletes projects without checking ownership.
The C# API uses Entity Framework and calls .Result on async methods; the list endpoint loads the whole table.
Our Python worker reads jobs from Postgres; two workers process the same job and the payment call happens inside the transaction.
The Kubernetes deployment for our Java service gets OOMKilled and its HashMap cache is shared across threads.
Our Svelte frontend loads data in +page.ts with an API key, and the PHP backend builds SQL from query strings.
An LLM agent with a shell tool runs in our CI; a pull request description told it to print the secrets.
Our Rust service writes to Redis; it stalls when reading files with std::fs and two instances both hold the same lock.
The Flutter app calls our Django REST API; setState runs after dispose and users can read other users' orders.
We run MongoDB and Elasticsearch-like search in our Node app; the aggregation is slow and deep pages use skip.
Our React app on Vercel ships a huge bundle because one chart library loads on every page, and the API route awaits three fetches in a row.
The Terraform config creates an S3 bucket that is public and hardcodes the database password.

tasks.task: Our product search lets people see every product, including unpublished ones, when they type something like ' OR '1'='1 into the search box. Searching for names with an apostrophe, like O'Brien's, also crashes. Fix search_products in store.py.

Our download endpoint calls read_upload(base_dir, name) from files.py with the name from the URL. A security report says someone downloaded ../config/secrets.env with it. Fix read_upload so it can only read files inside base_dir; it should raise PermissionError otherwise.

A security review flagged accounts.py: it stores passwords as plain SHA-256 hex digests, so two users with the same password get the same stored value and leaked hashes crack quickly. Make hash_password/verify_password safe with only the Python standard library. Existing callers only use these two functions.

Our API accepts tokens it should not: a pentester changed the user id inside a token and was let in, and another sent a token with "alg": "none". Tokens are HS256 JWTs signed with SECRET. Fix decode_token in tokens.py so it returns the claims only for genuine, unexpired tokens and raises InvalidToken otherwise.

After login we redirect to the ?next= parameter. Phishing emails now use our login link with next=https://evil.example to bounce users to a fake site. Fix safe_next in redirects.py: it should return the path when it stays on our site and '/' otherwise.
Someone posted a comment containing a <script> tag and it ran for every visitor. render_comment in render.py builds the HTML for one comment. Make it safe while keeping the same markup.

Our 'import image from URL' feature fetches whatever URL a user types. Someone used it to read our cloud metadata at http://169.254.169.254/ and an internal admin service. is_allowed_url(url, resolve) in fetcher.py is called before every fetch; resolve(host) returns the host's IP addresses. Make it reject URLs that would reach internal addresses.

An auditor showed they could predict our password-reset tokens after seeing a few of them. new_reset_token() in reset.py generates them. Make the tokens unpredictable; they are put in URLs, so they must stay URL-safe.

Our session cookie is a base64 pickle of the session dict (sessions.py). A researcher showed a crafted cookie runs code on our server, and users can also edit their own cookie to change user_id. Fix dump_session/load_session. load_session should return None for any cookie it does not trust. Sessions only hold JSON-friendly values.

find_duplicate_emails in dedupe.py was fine in testing, but on our real export of 60,000 customers it runs for many minutes. Make it fast; the output must not change (duplicates in order of their second appearance, compared case-insensitively, each reported once).

The monthly revenue report (customer_totals in report.py) got slower every month as we added customers; with a few thousand it now takes seconds and the database log is full of tiny queries. Make it efficient without changing its output.

Importing a 20,000-line CSV with import_events in importer.py takes minutes on our laptops' disks, and the database file is busy the whole time. Make the import fast. A failed import must not leave half the rows behind.

Our pricing worker's memory grows all day until it is OOM-killed; restarts make it go away for a while. price_for in pricing.py is called with many different (sku, region) pairs. Keep the caching benefit for repeated lookups but stop the growth. Keep at most about 10,000 entries.

load_dashboard in dashboard.py fetches 12 widgets and takes 12x as long as a single widget. Each fetch is an independent async call. Speed it up, but the widget API allows at most 4 requests in flight per client. Results must stay in input order.

Our async web service stops answering health checks whenever someone requests a report: render_report in service.py calls a slow synchronous library function (build_pdf). While one report renders, every other request waits. Fix it without changing render_report's result.

Our activity feed API pages through 200,000 events with list_events(conn, page, per_page) in feed.py. Page 1 is instant, but page 3,000 is slow and users scrolling while new events arrive see duplicates. Add list_events_after(conn, before=None, per_page=50) that returns (events, next_cursor) for newest-first pages, and make deep pages fast. Keep list_events working for old clients.

Signups occasionally hang a worker at 100% CPU for minutes. We traced it to is_valid_display_name in validate.py when people paste long names ending in a symbol. Fix it; the accepted names must stay the same: one or more words of letters/digits/underscore separated by single spaces, up to 40 characters.

When our homepage cache entry expires under load, dozens of threads recompute it at once and the database falls over. Fix get_or_compute in cache.py so that concurrent misses for the same key compute it once, while different keys do not wait for each other.

Our wallet balances sometimes go negative even though withdraw() in wallet.py checks the balance first. It happens when a user taps 'withdraw' several times quickly (requests run on parallel threads). Fix it.

Mobile clients retry POST /charges when the network times out, and some customers were charged twice. The client already sends an Idempotency-Key header with each logical payment. Update charge() in payments.py so a repeated key never charges again and returns the original result, even if the retries arrive at the same time.

call_with_retry in retry.py hammers our partner API in a tight loop forever when it is down, and it even retries on 'invalid request' errors that can never succeed. Make it retry only transient failures (ConnectionError and TimeoutError), at most 4 attempts in total, waiting with exponential backoff plus jitter between attempts (use the sleep argument), and re-raise the last error when it gives up.

Customers report invoice totals that are off by a cent, and our accountant says we must round each line's tax half-up to the cent (e.g. 0.125 -> 0.13) before summing. invoice_total in invoice.py takes prices as decimal strings. Make the totals exact; it should return a string with two decimals.

Our log scanner crashes with 'Too many open files' after a few hours. count_errors in logscan.py is called on thousands of files. Fix the leak, including when a file contains invalid bytes and decoding raises.

Our nightly sync job hangs forever when the partner API accepts the connection but never answers; we have to kill it by hand. fetch_status in client.py makes the call. Make it give up within 5 seconds by default (the caller may pass a different timeout) and raise TimeoutError so the job can move on.

list_orders in api.py backs GET /orders. A big customer has 80,000 orders and the endpoint now times out and uses gigabytes of memory. Change it to list_orders(store, customer_id, limit=None, cursor=None) returning {"items": [...], "next_cursor": str or None}: pages of 50 by default, never more than 100 per page even if the client asks, oldest first by id, with next_cursor None on the last page.

sync_contacts in sync.py reports success even when pushes to the CRM fail, so missing contacts go unnoticed for weeks, and Ctrl+C does not stop it. Make it keep going past individual failures, return the ids that failed, log each failure with its traceback via the module logger, and let KeyboardInterrupt stop the run.

Our ledger service occasionally freezes completely and has to be restarted. It started after we made transfer() in ledger.py thread-safe. Transfers between the same two accounts in opposite directions seem to be involved. Fix it; money must still never be created or lost.
search() in broken.py hangs forever on some inputs instead of returning. Fix it.
